mainTopic: Conditional vows about sleep and benefit: whether one must hold back now when a later act could make a vow take effect backward (רב יהודה)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a rule: a person may be careless about a condition (תנאי), but he is careful about a direct איסור. The גמרא then tests רב יהודה against the משנה of 'קונם שאני ישן'. Read literally, that cannot be a valid נדר, because sleep has no substance. So the גמרא tries 'קונם עיני בשינה'. A vow with no time limit cannot be kept, as רבי יוחנן taught. The גמרא then tries 'tomorrow if I sleep today', but that clashes with the rule that people are careful with a direct איסור. The final wording, 'today if I sleep tomorrow', seems to refute רב יהודה, and the גמרא answers that the משנה only speaks after the fact. רבינא instead keeps the plain wording and says the בל יחל is only rabbinic, proving from customs that a rabbinic בל יחל exists. Finally, the גמרא challenges רב יהודה from a משנה about a wife's conditional vow. רבי אבא answers, and the last clause of that משנה pushes back again, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: People are careless with conditions but careful with prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the earlier reasoning. A person may be careless about a condition, but he is careful about a direct prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person is only careless when it comes to a condition. When it comes to a direct prohibition, he is careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reasoning from just before this point. It explains why a vow worded as a direct prohibition worries us less than one worded as a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the forbidden act only makes a condition come true, a person may slip, because it does not feel forbidden at that moment. When the act itself is directly forbidden, he will be on guard. This distinction is the rule the גמרא will use against the next משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis of the קשיא in step 7.

phrases.english: For when a person is not careful, it is with a condition,
but with a prohibition he is careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is careless with a condition but careful with a direct prohibition.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about vowing not to sleep, walk or speak
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about vowing not to sleep, walk or speak, and asks what exact case it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'It is קונם that I sleep, that I walk, that I speak,' and so on. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a משנה and asks how to picture it. This sets up the next moves, which will lead to a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats these vows as valid. The גמרא wants to know the exact wording. The wording will decide whether the vow can work at all, and whether it fits the rule from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: a word used to make a vow, like קרבן: 'this is forbidden to me'
what are the circumstances? how do we picture the case?

phrases.english: We learned:
"Konam that I sleep,"
"that I walk," "that I speak," etc.
What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that will be tested against the rule in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact vow wording is the משנה describing?

steps.title: A vow on sleep should not work, since sleep has no substance
steps.stepSummary: If the vow is worded exactly as the משנה says, it should not be valid. נדרים only take effect on things with physical substance, and sleep has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the wording is just as the משנה says, is 'that I sleep' a vow at all? We learned that oaths are stricter: they take effect on things with substance and on things without substance, but vows do not. And sleep has no substance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries reading the משנה literally and finds a problem: a vow cannot take hold of sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר forbids an object (חפצא), while a שבועה binds the person (גברא). That is why a שבועה works on things without substance and a נדר does not. Sleep is an action, not an object, so the literal wording cannot be a valid נדר.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (the first suggestion, which is about to be rejected)
a way that oaths are stricter than vows

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up שבועה and נדר here. A שבועה can apply to sleep, but a נדר cannot, unless it is tied to something physical.

phrases.english: If we say it is as it is taught,
is "that I sleep" a vow?
But didn't we learn: there is a stringency with oaths,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַשְּׁבוּעוֹת חָלוֹת עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ
phrases.english: that oaths take effect on something that has substance
and on something that has no substance,
which is not so with vows.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֵׁינָה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ הוּא!
phrases.english: And sleep is something that has no substance!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא כִּדְקָתָנֵי שֶׁאֲנִי יָשֵׁן מִי הָוֵי נִדְרָא וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the literal reading as an answer to step 2 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of the משנה, 'קונם שאני ישן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נדרים do not take effect on things without substance, and sleep has no substance, so the literal wording cannot be a valid vow.

steps.title: He tied the vow to his eyes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means he said 'my eyes are קונם for sleep.' This ties the vow to something physical.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he said: 'My eyes are קונם for sleep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by changing the wording of the vow. He attached the vow to his eyes, which are a physical object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His eyes are a real object, so the נדר can take hold of them. It forbids his eyes from being used for sleeping. Now the vow is valid.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he said:
"My eyes are konam for sleep."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 3 by changing the vow's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow was worded 'קונם שאני ישן', which cannot be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow was 'קונם עיני בשינה', which ties it to a physical object.

steps.title: A vow never to sleep cannot be kept
steps.stepSummary: If he set no time limit, the vow forbids sleep forever, and he is sure to break it. רבי יוחנן teaches that an oath like this does not hold, and he may sleep right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set no time limit, do we leave him until he breaks 'he shall not profane his word'? But רבי יוחנן said: someone who swears 'I will not sleep for three days' gets lashes, and he may sleep right away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new wording. A vow never to sleep is impossible to keep, so it should not take effect at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one can go without sleep for long. רבי יוחנן says even three days is impossible, so that oath is a שבועת שוא, an oath sworn for nothing: he gets lashes and may sleep immediately. So a vow with no time limit cannot be what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: a limit or measure (here, a time limit)
the prohibition against breaking one's word

phrases.english: And if he did not give a limit,
do we leave him alone
until he transgresses the prohibition "he shall not profane"?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
"An oath that I will not sleep for three days":
they give him lashes, and he may sleep immediately!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי דְּלָא יָהֵיב שִׁיעוּרָא מִי שָׁבְקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'קונם עיני בשינה' with no time limit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a vow is impossible to keep. Based on רבי יוחנן, it does not bind him at all, so the משנה cannot be talking about it.

steps.title: A vow about tomorrow, depending on sleeping today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now says the vow was: 'my eyes are קונם for sleep tomorrow if I sleep today.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he said: 'My eyes are קונם for sleep tomorrow if I sleep today.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the case again. Now the vow has a time limit and a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This vow can be kept, because it only forbids one day of sleep. The משנה, which forbids him to sleep, would then mean he should not sleep today, so that he does not end up breaking the vow tomorrow.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he said:
"My eyes are konam for sleep tomorrow
if I sleep today."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דַּאֲמַר קֻוֽנָּם עֵינַי בְּשֵׁינָה לְמָחָר אִם אִישַׁן הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 5 by adding a time limit and a condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow forbade sleep forever and could not be kept.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow forbids sleep only tomorrow, and only if he sleeps today.

steps.title: But you said a person is careful with a direct prohibition
steps.stepSummary: This new case contradicts the rule from step 1. Sleeping tomorrow would be a direct איסור, and a person is careful with that, so why stop him from sleeping today?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said that anyone facing a direct prohibition is careful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the rule from step 1 against the last answer. In this case he should be allowed to sleep today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In 'tomorrow if I sleep today', sleeping today only makes the condition true. The forbidden act, sleeping tomorrow, is a direct איסור, and step 1 said a person watches himself with that. So there is no reason to forbid sleeping today, and the משנה, which forbids it, cannot be this case.

keyTerms.meaning: but you said (pointing out a contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא went through three readings of the משנה: (1) 'קונם שאני ישן' fails because sleep has no substance; (2) 'קונם עיני בשינה' with no limit fails because it cannot be kept; (3) 'tomorrow if I sleep today' clashes with the rule that a person is careful with a direct איסור.

phrases.english: But you said
that anyone with his prohibition is careful?
phrases.notes: This points back to the rule in step 1: people watch themselves with a direct prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 6 using the rule from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'קונם עיני בשינה למחר אם אישן היום'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this case the forbidden act is a direct איסור, and a person is careful with that, so sleeping today should be allowed. That contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: Flipping the vow: today's sleep depends on tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers step 7 by reversing the vow: 'my eyes are קונם for sleep today if I sleep tomorrow.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be that he said: 'My eyes are קונם for sleep today if I sleep tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new wording of the vow to escape the problem from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, sleeping tomorrow was the forbidden act itself, and a person is careful about that. Now the forbidden thing is today's sleep, and it only becomes forbidden later, if he sleeps tomorrow. That is not a direct איסור at the moment he acts, so he may not be careful, and the warning in the משנה makes sense.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that he said:
"My eyes are konam for sleep today
if I sleep tomorrow."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by reversing which day's sleep is forbidden.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (new wording of the vow)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow forbade sleep tomorrow, which is a direct איסור that a person is careful with.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow forbids today's sleep only if he later sleeps tomorrow, so the איסור is not direct and a warning is needed.

steps.title: The new wording seems to refute רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה warns about sleeping tomorrow, which only matters if he already slept today. That suggests he may sleep today, against רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not sleep today, then when he sleeps tomorrow, what בל יחל is there? It must be talking about where he did sleep today. So there is a case where he sleeps today. This refutes רב יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new wording. It seems to clash with רב יהודה, who says he may not sleep today in case he sleeps tomorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sleeping tomorrow only causes בל יחל if he already slept today, since only then does today's sleep become forbidden. So the משנה's warning seems to picture someone who slept today. That suggests sleeping today is allowed from the start, which goes against רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: "He shall not profane his word", the Torah ban on breaking a vow

phrases.english: And if he does not sleep today,
when he sleeps tomorrow,
what "he shall not profane his word" is there?
Rather, is it not where he did sleep [today]?
So apparently there is a case where he sleeps.
And this is a refutation of Rav Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the wording from step 8 and draws out what it implies: the משנה pictures someone who slept today, which refutes רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that he may not sleep today in case he sleeps tomorrow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's warning only makes sense if he slept today, so it seems to picture sleeping today as normal and allowed.

steps.title: The משנה means only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking of a case where he already slept today. It does not mean he is allowed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה teaches this, it means: if he did sleep today, he may not sleep tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה. The משנה is not permitting sleep today; it only says what to do if he already slept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the משנה pictures sleeping today as allowed. The answer reads it as after the fact: today he should not sleep, but if he did, he must be careful tomorrow. So רב יהודה stands.
steps.whatToRemember: With the wording 'קונם for sleep today if I sleep tomorrow,' רב יהודה says don't sleep today. The משנה's warning is only for someone who already did.

phrases.english: When it teaches [this], it means if he did sleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's refutation of רב יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה as after the fact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה pictures sleeping today as allowed from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only says what to do if he already slept today; from the start, he should not.

steps.title: רבינא: the plain wording, with a rabbinic בל יחל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא keeps the משנה's plain wording. He says the vow does not truly take effect, and the בל יחל is only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Actually, the משנה means just what it says ('קונם is sleep for me'). And what is the 'בל יחל' it mentions? It is a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a completely different answer. He goes back to the first problem in step 3 instead of changing the vow's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 said a vow on sleep is not valid because sleep has no physical substance. רבינא agrees that it does not work מדאורייתא. But the חכמים still forbade him to break his word, so the בל יחל in the משנה is rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught, in its plain wording

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying the vow takes effect. He agrees that by Torah law it does not; the ban on breaking it is only rabbinic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the need for all the reworded vows in steps 4–10, by treating the משנה's case as a rabbinic-level vow.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, it is as it teaches,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's own wording, 'קונם is sleep for me,' with no extra words about eyes or days.

phrases.english: and what is "he shall not profane"?
It is by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the reworded vows aside and answers the original קשיא of step 3 differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Lowering the level of the prohibition (Torah to rabbinic)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בל יחל in the משנה is Torah-level, so the vow must take effect by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow does not take effect by Torah law; the בל יחל is rabbinic.

steps.title: Is there such a thing as a rabbinic בל יחל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether בל יחל can exist on a rabbinic level at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really a בל יחל that is only rabbinic?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבינא's idea and sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל יחל is a Torah verse about vows. So it sounds strange to speak of a rabbinic version of it. The גמרא wants a source showing this exists.

phrases.english: But is there a "he shall not profane" by rabbinic law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the idea רבינא relied on in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the concept of בל יחל can apply on a rabbinic level.

steps.title: Proof from customs: rabbinic בל יחל exists
steps.stepSummary: Yes. A ברייתא says you may not permit something people treat as forbidden by custom, and it quotes 'לא יחל דברו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. A ברייתא teaches: things that are permitted, but some people have a custom to treat as forbidden, you may not permit in front of them, as it says, 'He shall not profane his word.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes and brings a ברייתא as proof, which supports רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A custom of holding back from something allowed is not a real Torah vow. Still, the ברייתא applies 'לא יחל דברו' to it. So the verse can be used on a rabbinic level, just as רבינא said.
steps.whatToRemember: רבינא: 'קונם is sleep for me' does not take effect by Torah law, but breaking it violates a rabbinic בל יחל. A rabbinic בל יחל exists, as with customs people keep.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the rule that a custom of holding back from something allowed has a binding force like a vow.

phrases.english: Yes, and it was taught in a baraita:
Matters that are permitted
but others have a custom of treating them as forbidden,
you may not permit them in their presence,
as it is stated: "He shall not profane his word."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12's question and backs up רבינא's approach.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A ברייתא applies 'לא יחל דברו' to customs, which are not Torah vows.

steps.title: A משנה about a wife's conditional vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a husband forbids his wife to benefit from him until פסח if she goes to her father's house before סוכות. If she went before פסח, she is forbidden until פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: A husband says, 'Benefit from me is forbidden to you until פסח, if you go to your father's house before סוכות.' If she went before פסח, she may not benefit from him until פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a משנה to set up a new challenge against רב יהודה. This step only lays out the case. The attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow has two time frames. The ban on benefit lasts until פסח, but the condition (visiting her father) runs all the way to סוכות. So she could break the condition after פסח, which would make the vow take effect backward for the time before פסח. This is the same kind of case רב יהודה dealt with.

keyTerms.meaning: You benefit (here, a vow forbidding benefit)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two dates. The ban lasts only until פסח, but the condition (going to her father's house) stays open until סוכות.

phrases.english: We learned: 'That you benefit from me until פסח
phrases.notes: This is vow language. He means: benefit from me is forbidden to you until פסח.

phrases.aramaic: אִם תֵּלְכִי לְבֵית אָבִיךְ עַד הֶחָג״,
phrases.english: if you go to your father's house until the Festival,'
if she went before פסח —
she is forbidden to benefit from him until פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: שֶׁאַתְּ נֶהֱנֵית לִי עַד הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier challenge was settled, the גמרא brings a new source to test רב יהודה again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she went to her father's house before פסח, she is forbidden to benefit from her husband until פסח.

steps.title: If she did not go, she may benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. Only if she went is she forbidden, so if she has not gone she may benefit. That goes against רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she went before פסח, she is forbidden. If she did not go, she is not forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the משנה's wording and uses it as a challenge to רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids her only after she went. That suggests that before she goes, she may benefit freely, even though she might still go later (before סוכות) and make the vow take effect backward. רב יהודה said you must hold back in exactly that kind of case.

phrases.english: If she went before פסח — she is forbidden,
if she did not go — not!
phrases.notes: Meaning she is not forbidden. That is the problem for רב יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלְכָה לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח — אֲסוּרָה, לֹא הָלְכָה — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה, who forbids benefit now when a later act could make the vow take effect backward.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids her only once she went. So before she goes she may benefit, even though the condition is still open.

steps.title: רבי אבא: Before she goes, still forbidden but no lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains the משנה. If she went, she is forbidden and gets מלקות. If she has not gone, she is still forbidden, just without lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: If she went before פסח, she is forbidden and is lashed. If she did not go, she is simply forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא defends רב יהודה. He says the משנה's 'forbidden' means a ban that brings lashes, while a plain ban still applies before she goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא reads the משנה as a contrast between two levels of ban, not between forbidden and allowed. Once she went, the vow is fully in force, so benefiting brings מלקות. Before that she must still hold back, as רב יהודה says, but there are no lashes.

phrases.english: רבי אבא said:
If she went before פסח — she is forbidden, and is lashed.
If she did not go — she is merely forbidden.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the משנה's contrast as two levels of ban (with lashes or without), not forbidden versus allowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Before she goes to her father's house, she may benefit freely.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before she goes she is still forbidden, just without lashes. So the משנה fits רב יהודה.

steps.title: The end of the משנה shows she benefited
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says that if she goes after פסח, there is בל יחל. That only works if she already benefited before פסח, so it seems she was allowed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: if she goes after פסח, it falls under 'he shall not break his word.' But if she did not benefit before פסח, how could there be בל יחל? It must be that she did benefit. So apparently she may benefit...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבא's answer using the last part of the same משנה. The sentence continues on the next amud, but the challenge is already clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she goes to her father's house between פסח and סוכות, the vow takes effect backward on the time before פסח. That breaks the vow only if she actually benefited before פסח. Since the משנה treats this as a normal case, she seems to have been allowed to benefit, which goes against רבי אבא and רב יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This puts רב יהודה's view under real pressure again, because the proof comes from the משנה's own last clause.

phrases.english: Say the last part:
After פסח, it is under 'he shall not break his word.'
phrases.notes: Meaning: if she goes to her father's house after פסח, there is a violation of בל יחל (במדבר 30:3).

phrases.english: And if she did not benefit before פסח,
is there 'he shall not break'?
Rather, it is obvious that she benefited.
Apparently, she may benefit,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud. The point is that she was allowed to benefit before פסח.
